name: games3d
description: Browser games (2D canvas or Three.js) and 3D models: design, build, play-test in a real headless browser, independent playtest/art review, glTF export with validation; Blender and Godot through the engine-blender and engine-godot plugins (their tools, gates, skills and agents). Needs the visual plugin.

views.title: Studio
views.description: Games and 3D at a glance: recent projects, running and recent jobs, the engines on this machine and their gaps, quick starts.

views.title: Projects
views.description: Every Studio project (.studio/project.json) in your folders; params {"project": id or folder} opens one: its stages to approve or comment on, the design document, builds, playtests and assets.

views.title: Assets
views.description: The assets of every project and the shared library as a grid with previews, filtered by kind, dimension, style, license and source; params {"asset": ref} opens one with its provenance, license, checks and files.

views.title: Scenes
views.description: Engine scenes and levels of the projects (Godot .tscn with their node outline, Unreal .umap, Unity .unity, .blend, glTF scenes, level JSON).

views.title: Renders
views.description: Renders, previews, turntables and captures, newest first; pick two to compare side by side.

views.title: Builds
views.description: Builds of every project with their status; params {"project", "id"} opens one with its log and the problems in it, linked to the source lines.

views.title: Playtests
views.description: Playtest reports; params {"project", "id"} opens one: the timeline with frames and events, metrics charts against the budgets, issues with evidence, verdicts and the recording.

views.title: Jobs
views.description: The heavy-job queue (renders, builds, cooks, bakes, long plays): running, waiting and the last hour's, with cancel.

views.title: Engines
views.description: Blender, Godot, Unreal, Unity and the web on this machine: installed or not, versions, toolchain gaps, and how to install what is missing.

views.title: 3D viewer
views.description: An interactive viewer for a .glb or .gltf: orbit, wireframe, normals, UV checker, LOD switch, the animation player, size and triangle stats.

views.title: 2D viewer
views.description: Sprites and sprite sheets (frames, playback at a frame rate, nearest-neighbour zoom, grid), tilesets and levels (Tiled .tmj or level JSON drawn with their tileset).

views.title: Audio player
views.description: Sound effects and music with their waveform: play, loop, seek.

input.idea: A 2D side-scrolling platformer: run, jump and collect coins across three short levels, enemies to stomp, a goal flag; pixel-art style, keyboard controls (arrows/WASD, space to jump).

agent.description: Opens the build-game workflow dialog for a 2D platformer (the person confirms and picks the folder).

input.idea: A 3D third-person collect-and-escape game: one level, collectibles, a score UI, a win condition and an exit door that opens after the last collectible; a follow camera, WASD to move, space to jump.

agent.description: Opens the build-game workflow dialog for a 3D third-person game (engine browser; the person can choose godot).
Opens the model-3d workflow dialog (the person describes the model and picks three or blender).

action.prompt: Make a sprite sheet with Studio: a character walk cycle of 8 frames at 32x32 pixels, pixel-art, transparent background. Save it as a Studio asset (.studio/assets/<id>/ with asset.json: kind spritesheet, frames, frameSize, fps) and show it in the 2D viewer.

agent.description: Types a prompt for the person in a new chat: make a sprite sheet as a Studio asset.

action.prompt: Generate a level with Studio: a 2D tile level (40x20 tiles of 16 px) with a start, a goal, platforms, gaps and a few enemies, from a tileset. Save it as a Studio asset of kind level (level JSON or a Tiled .tmj with its tileset) and show it in the 2D viewer.

agent.description: Types a prompt for the person in a new chat: generate a level as a Studio asset.

action.prompt: Install Godot 4 for Studio: use the Godot engine tool's install action (the official build into ~/.harness/engines, checksums verified). Ask me before downloading anything, then run detect and tell me what it found.

Install Blender for Studio: use the Blender engine tool's install action if it has one, else tell me the exact command for this system (winget, brew or the official download) and wait for me to run it. Then run detect.

Make a game with Studio: {args}

Load the games3d-guide skill first. Pick the engine from what is installed (Studio > Engines), keep the project in .studio/project.json with its stages, and playtest it before calling it done.
